Source: Diamond Spheres: Erudition & Esoterica

Prerequisites: Nature sphere ((plant) package), Plant Mastery.

Benefit: You can use fungi and dead plant life instead of the normal requirements for your plant package abilities. Additionally, you gain the following additions or improvements to the corresponding Nature sphere abilities and talents.

  • Create Nature: When you use Create Nature to grow plants, you can instead grow patches of fungus. When you do, you can reduce the spell point cost by 1 (minimum 0) if you use a Medium-sized or larger corpse as its source—this causes rapid decay to the corpse, effectively destroying it for the purposes of returning the creature to life and making it unable to be used as a source a second time using this ability.
  • Entangle: If you create an Entangle effect within an area of fungi, all creatures suffer 1 acid damage each round they remain within the area.
  • Harvest: When you produce magical berries using Harvest with Plant Mastery, you can instead produce 3 magical mushrooms per caster level—in addition to their normal effects, a creature that consumes a magical mushroom gains a +1 bonus to saving throws against illusion and mind-affecting effects for 1 hour.
  • Hazardous Terrain: When using Entangle, instead of causing the effect to grow thorns, you can have the plants grow corrosive growths, dealing acid damage equal to 1d6 + your caster level per round to all creatures within the area. A successful Reflex save against this Entangle effect also halves this damage.
  • Pummel Mastery—Mycotoxic Miasma: Instead of a regular attack, you can instruct an animated branch to produce a thick haze of toxic spores. All creatures adjacent to the branch must succeed at a Fortitude save or become sickened and have all of their speeds halved for 1 round. This is a poison effect. If you also have the Thrown Pummel talent, the branch can throw these spores (with a range increment equal to twice their reach), affecting a 5-foot cube.
  • Nature’s Carapace: While under the effects of the Barkskin effect, whenever you are damaged by a melee attack, the attacker suffers an amount of acid damage equal to twice your caster level (Fortitude negates).
  • Nature’s Weapon—Spore Cloud: As a standard action you can release a cloud of spores in a 15-foot cone. All creatures within the area suffer 1d4 acid damage per caster level and become sickened for 1d4 rounds—a successful Fortitude save halves this damage and negates the sickened condition. This is a poison effect.
  • Wreath of Elements—Fungal Fortitude: You fortify yourself, gaining a +2 alchemical bonus to a single saving throw, increasing by +1 per 5 caster levels. Alternatively, if you use this ability after succeeding a Fortitude saving throw against an effect that has a partial effect on a successful save, you instead suffer no effect.

Source: Spheres of Power Wiki
